items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed with effort.
The sphere of concealment is the mortal world.
The specific group named is the lowest of men.
items.inference: This teaching must be diligently hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: What kind of recipient is qualified to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient is described as previously accomplished.
The recipient must be tested for one year.
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is fit to receive it.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa.
The section is numbered as fifth.
The section is called a chapter.
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of Kaula been understood?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas.
Understanding occurred by that lord's grace.
What is known is the determination of Kaula.
items.inference: The speaker has understood the determination of Kaula through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of Kaulas, by your grace I have understood the determination of Kaula.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The question asks who the declared soul is.
It also asks what the soul's nature is.
Both identity and nature are under inquiry.
items.inference: The verse seeks clarification of both the soul's identity and its essential nature.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The question asks where dissolution occurs.
The soul is said to go to dissolution.
The speaker requests a complete explanation.
items.inference: The verse asks for a full account of the locus into which the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme.
It is described as partless and eternal.
It is free from disease and stain.
items.inference: The soul's true nature is supreme, partless, eternal, and untainted.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme.
That same soul is identified as haṃsa.
It is also characterized as power and individual.
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The subject is the air filled with breath.
It is described as situated.
Its location is in all beings.
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body.
At that point the soul is designated anew.
The designation given is supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching said to be received through traditional transmission?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear.
It comes down through a lineage sequence.
The goddess is addressed as recipient.
items.inference: The teaching is received aurally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge, fair-faced one?
premises: The cause is this knowledge alone.
The knowledge is received by hearing.
The fair-faced one is addressed.
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge has a significant effect.
uncertainties: The verse states the cause but leaves the result to be completed in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: The practice is to be undertaken for six months.
The practitioner is described as one who practices.
The goal is a state free from bondage.
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The exact sense of kāṣāyaṃ in this context is uncertain.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What two results follow from the prescribed practice for the practitioner?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases.
The practitioner gains union with yogis.
Both results are presented together.
items.inference: The practice yields freedom from all diseases and communion with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī.
The content communicated is the practice of the soul.
The communication is declared complete.
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved person may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient is endowed with all states.
The recipient has a resolved mind.
items.inference: It may be given to a person of resolved mind who is endowed with all states.
uncertainties: The phrase sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is doctrinally broad and somewhat ambiguous.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.

items.question: To whom must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given?
premises: The Kaula essence is not to be given.
This essence originates from the yoginīs.
The prohibition is stated emphatically.
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching that originates from the yoginīs must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The intended recipient of the prohibition is implicit rather than explicitly named.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the speaker's body is claimed after receiving knowledge?
premises: The speaker refers to her body now.
The body is described as pure.
It was previously struck by the veil of ignorance.
items.inference: The speaker claims her body is now pure, having been freed from the veil of ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, no longer struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish to hear.
The topic is the overcoming of time.
This overcoming is described as auspicious.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious method for overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through the teaching?
premises: The speaker promises to explain.
There is said to be no doubt.
The result is that death is destroyed.
items.inference: The teaching will explain without doubt how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you; there is no doubt, as to how death is destroyed.

items.question: What paradoxical condition affects even the wise at the tip of nectar?
premises: The context involves the tip of nectar.
There is contact with the essence-tip.
Even a wise person is described as burning.
items.inference: Even the wise may experience a burning condition at the tip of nectar.
uncertainties: The imagery of burning at the nectar-tip is obscure and may be technical.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one burns at the tip of nectar, by the tip of its essence.

items.question: How should the practitioner draw in the vital air at the tongue and palate root?
premises: The action is located at the root of tongue and palate.
The practitioner should take in the air.
The action must be done slowly.
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly draw in the air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this method for one full year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year.
The condition is that it has been practiced.
The stated result is destruction of old age and death.
items.inference: Practicing this method for one year destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to serpent venom results from the completed practice?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison does not enter the body.
The immunity is stated as a direct result.
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the practitioner's body.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
